items.title: 52300_Trummy Young oral history interview
items.q: I had another band on 52nd Street with Dexter Gordon playing tenor sax, and Jimmy Jones playing piano.

ctx.x: And Jimmy Jones used to tell me stories about Duke because Jimmy got very close to him in later years, you know. He says -- he says he never saw Duke when he wasn't either thinking of a tune or writing a tune or humming something. He says he never saw him when he wasn't in that frame of mind. And that's --
He'd have little scraps of paper. He'd jot things down -- in his pockets, and as soon as there was a portable piano invented, he had one in his hotel room, a little Wurlitzer.

items.title: 69537_Jimmy Jones oral history interview
items.q: We had a full rhythm section, Trummy and I forget who was -- who was playing with us... Trummy would come out to the house... work over some things at the piano... we had a big orchestra with... Trummy Young

ctx.x: How big a group was it?
We had a full rhythm section, Trummy and I forget who was -- who was playing with us in the front line. It was about, you know, five or six or seven pieces, something like that.
